title: 27yo F Anaphylaxis
chiefComplaint: Rash and difficulty breathing after a meal
background: Brought in by friends 20 minutes after eating shrimp fried rice at a street stall. She developed itching in her palms, then a spreading rash, throat tightness and vomiting. She has known allergic rhinitis and mild asthma, uses salbutamol MDI once or twice a month. She carries no adrenaline autoinjector. She took cetirizine 10 mg at the restaurant with no improvement. Last menstrual period 2 weeks ago.

exam.finding: Anxious, sitting upright, flushed and diaphoretic, speaking in short phrases
Swollen lips and tongue, hoarse voice, audible inspiratory stridor, no drooling, mouth opening adequate, Mallampati now III from tongue swelling
Sinus tachycardia, thready radial pulse, capillary refill 4 seconds, no murmur, JVP flat
Diffuse expiratory wheeze in all fields, prolonged expiratory phase, suprasternal and intercostal retractions, poor air entry at both bases
Soft, mild diffuse tenderness without guarding, hyperactive bowel sounds, one episode of vomiting in triage
Generalised confluent urticaria over trunk and limbs, warm flushed periphery over a cool clammy forehead, no purpura
GCS 14 (E4V4M6), agitated and frightened, no focal deficit, pupils 4 mm equal and reactive

investigations.name: 12-Lead ECG
investigations.report: Sinus tachycardia at 126/min. No ischaemic ST changes. Normal QTc.

investigations.name: Portable Chest X-ray
investigations.report: Hyperinflated lung fields with flattened hemidiaphragms. No consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Normal cardiac silhouette.

investigations.name: Capillary glucose
investigations.report: Normal. Excludes hypoglycaemia as a cause of altered behaviour.

investigations.name: Arterial blood gas (room air)
investigations.report: Hypoxaemia with metabolic acidosis and partial respiratory compensation, consistent with shock and bronchospasm.

investigations.name: Lactate
investigations.report: Elevated, consistent with distributive shock and hypoperfusion.

investigations.name: Serum tryptase (acute)
investigations.report: Markedly raised. Confirmatory only, resulted after the resuscitation. Repeat a baseline level at 24 hours.

investigations.name: Haematocrit
investigations.report: Haemoconcentration from capillary leak and plasma extravasation.

data.label: Sit at eye level, tell her what is happening and that you are giving adrenaline now (Empathy)
data.narrative: You take 15 seconds to explain the plan in plain language while the nurse draws up adrenaline. Her respiratory rate settles slightly as the panic drops. Her friend hands over the packaging from the meal, which lists shrimp paste and peanut oil.

data.label: IM adrenaline to the anterolateral thigh

doseMap.Adrenaline (epinephrine) 1 mg/mL IM: 0.5 mg (0.5 mL of 1:1000) IM mid anterolateral thigh, repeat every 5 min as needed

data.label: High flow oxygen and position supine with legs raised
Two large bore IV lines and rapid crystalloid bolus

doseMap.Normal saline bolus: 20 mL/kg (about 1000 mL) over 10-15 min, reassess after each bolus

data.label: Partial response
data.narrative: Stridor softens and the urticaria starts to fade. She is still wheezing and remains hypotensive after the first litre.

data.label: Second IM adrenaline dose at 5 minutes for persistent hypotension

doseMap.Adrenaline (epinephrine) 1 mg/mL IM (rep: 0.5 mg IM, then start IV infusion if a third dose is needed

doseMap.Salbutamol nebuliser: 2.5 mg in 3 mL saline, driven by oxygen, repeat as needed

data.label: Adjuncts after adrenaline, never instead of it
Stabilised
data.narrative: Stridor resolves, wheeze clears to scattered end-expiratory squeaks, and the rash is fading. She is talking in full sentences.

data.label: Admit for observation and arrange discharge safety net
actions: Allergy clinic referral and 24h baseline tryptase

doseMap.Prescribe 2 adrenaline autoinjectors: 0.3 mg autoinjector, demonstrate technique before discharge

data.label: Disposition
data.narrative: She is observed for 8 hours with no biphasic reaction. She leaves with two autoinjectors, an action plan, and an allergy clinic appointment. Her friend photographs the stall sign so she can avoid it.
